El nombre interno dice «No Simbólicas», pero es de magnitudes simbólicas. - **10750.** 40 pares, 60 s; autoaplicada. - **2006.** 27 pares de números: el niño dice cuál es mayor. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=3} ![10747 · Magnitudes Simbólicas](../../figuras/plataforma/10747.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 10747"} ![10750 · Magnitudes Simbólicas](../../figuras/plataforma/10750.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 10750"} ![2006 · Magnitudes Simbólicas - Subitizing](../../figuras/plataforma/2006.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2006"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Comparing quantities measures **numerical magnitude processing**. In the **non-symbolic** version, the child sees two sets of dots and says whether they have the same number or not: this is attributed to the approximate number system, which estimates quantities without counting. In the **symbolic** version, the child compares two digits and chooses the larger: this requires accessing magnitude from the learned symbol. **What the evidence says:** - **Both are related to mathematics, the symbolic one somewhat more.** A meta-analysis of 45 articles (284 effects, 17,201 participants) estimates r = .30 for symbolic comparison and .24 for non-symbolic comparison. The relation is stronger with mental calculation and early mathematics [@schneider2017associations]. - **Symbolic knowledge better predicts arithmetic progress.** In 6-year-olds followed for 11 months, knowledge of Arabic numerals predicted arithmetic growth and magnitude comparison added nothing [@gobel2014arithmetic]. In 62 Spanish 4-year-olds, digits and arithmetic predicted later improvement of the approximate system, and not the other way round [@munez2024interrelations]. - **The dot task is not a pure measure.** Most children compare the sets by their visual features (size, area) more than by number [@clayton2019nonsymbolic]. The evidence for the approximate system as a causal basis of arithmetic is contradictory. Symbolic comparison is the strongest candidate for school screening. **What our data show.** - **Reliability.** The non-symbolic version has modest consistency (α = .63) and little stability across terms (ρ = .29–.38); the symbolic version, even less (ρ = .20–.21). At age 5, 25% of children reach the maximum in the non-symbolic version. - **Validity against mathematics.** They predict low arithmetic at ages 10–11 poorly (AUC .54–.61). Symbolic comparison at ages 10–11 correlates with arithmetic at the same time point (r = .32–.39) ([Numerical cognition](../../cognicion-numerica.en.qmd#sec-mate-criterio)). - **Validity against reading.** They are related to low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency as much as or more than to arithmetic (AUC .57–.70 for concurrent symbolic comparison; up to .77 for non-symbolic at age 5, with only 22 cases). They may reflect speed or attention more than number sense. The grouped codes are not homogeneous: the non-symbolic task mixes an examiner-administered version (1744) and a self-administered one (10752), and code 1745 is a number line task, not a comparison task. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|-----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.1| 2006| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 352| 13| 339| 21| | 5.2| 2006| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 896| 0| 896| 35| | 5.3| 2006| 2012| 192|2017/18 | 342| 338| 0| 16| | 6.1| 2006| 2013| 898|2019/20 | 558| 401| 157| 35| | 6.2| 2006| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 911| 265| 646| 34| | 6.2| 10750| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 224| 0| 24| 8| | 7.1| 10750| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 257| 0| 0| 8| | 9.2| 10750| 2012| 949|2021/22 | 388| 75| 0| 11| | 10.2| 10747| 2011| 948|2021/22 | 415| 0| 316| 14| | 11.2| 10747| 2010| 948|2021/22 | 416| 46| 227| 15| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |-----:|----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 2006| 5.3| 338| 2012| 21.96| 5.39| 25| -1.00| 0.00| 1.48| | 2006| 6.1| 401| 2013| 22.40| 5.34| 26| -1.04| 0.00| 1.25| | 2006| 6.2| 265| 2010| 23.83| 4.13| 26| -1.86| 0.00| 1.51| | 10750| 9.2| 75| 2012| 34.77| 6.78| 37| -1.99| 0.00| 24.00| | 10747| 11.2| 46| 2010| 31.20| 10.50| 35| -1.22| 2.17| 2.17| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. LEEDUCA battery) assesses symbolic number sense. The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 11 sessions, from 5 to 11 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Stability across time points was ρ = .20–.21. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .51–.63. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 9.2 (form 10750) (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - The task has 3 forms; in 1 of 1 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
